content: The text provided appears to be a detailed and technical description of a questionnaire or survey module related to various aspects of HIV prevention, care, treatment, and associated factors such as stigma, discrimination, and violence. 1. Cotrimoxazole Use and Recommendations Cotrimoxazole, also known as Cotrim, is recommended for individuals living with HIV (PLHIV) who present with a CD4 count below 350 or symptomatic disease (classified as stage 3 or 4). It is included in the advanced HIV disease package and is used to prevent certain opportunistic infections. However, it is important to note that Cotrimoxazole does not treat HIV itself. Have you ever taken Cotrimoxazole? Are you currently taking Cotrimoxazole? 2. CD4 Testing and Results CD4 testing measures the immune system's strength in individuals with HIV. Have you ever had your CD4 count tested? What was the result of your most recent CD4 test? What was your last CD4 count? 3. Antiretroviral Therapy (ART) ART, also known as ARVs, is the cornerstone of HIV treatment. Are you currently taking ARVs? If not, what is the main reason you have never taken ARVs? For those who have started ART, in which year and month did you begin treatment? 4. Viral Load Testing Viral load testing measures the amount of HIV in the blood. Have you ever had a viral load test? If not, why have you not undergone this test? When was your last viral load test? What were the results of your last viral load test? Results are typically categorized as suppressed (indicating very low or undetectable levels of the virus) or not suppressed (indicating significant viral presence). 5. Tuberculosis (TB) Screening and Treatment TB is a common co-infection in individuals with HIV. In the past 12 months, have you undergone a chest X-ray or sputum test to screen for TB? What was the result of your most recent TB test? 6. Cervical Cancer Screening Cervical cancer screening is essential for women, particularly those living with HIV. Have you ever been screened for cervical cancer? If not, what are the reasons for not undergoing screening? For those screened, did you receive treatment following the screening? 7. Pre-Exposure Prophylaxis (PrEP) and Post-Exposure Prophylaxis (PEP) PrEP is a preventive medication for HIV-negative individuals to reduce the risk of acquiring HIV. PEP is a short-term treatment taken after potential exposure to HIV. Have you heard of PrEP or PEP? Have you ever taken PrEP or PEP? If you have taken PrEP, how often do you take it, and where do you usually obtain it? If you have taken PEP, what was the reason for taking it? 8. Stigma, Discrimination, and Violence Stigma and discrimination are significant barriers to HIV prevention, care, and treatment. Have you experienced stigma or discrimination related to your HIV status or behaviors? Have you experienced physical or sexual violence in the past 12 months due to your HIV status or behaviors? If so, what services did you access to address these experiences? 9. Key Populations and Vulnerabilities The questionnaire also addresses specific challenges faced by key populations, including sex workers, men who have sex with men (MSM), transgender individuals, people who inject drugs (PWID), and other vulnerable groups. Questions are tailored to capture experiences of stigma, harassment, and discrimination specific to these populations. If a participant belongs to multiple key populations, questions are repeated to understand intersecting stigmas. 10. Programmatic Interventions The data collected from this questionnaire is intended to inform programmatic interventions aimed at reducing barriers to HIV prevention, care, and treatment. This includes addressing internalized stigma, experienced stigma, and discrimination.
